architecture.mechanism: Apparent perpetual motion always resolves to either a hidden external energy input (the system is not isolated) or an assumption that violates the first or second law of thermodynamics; real machines also lose energy to friction and other nonconservative forces.
architecture.intervention: Conduct a full energy audit of the water-powered car by metering every input (water chemistry, ambient heat, any electromagnetic or mechanical input) and every output (shaft work, heat, friction, exhaust), then either locate and disclose the hidden external source or supply a legitimate external energy input; infinite mileage on a single glass of water is rejected unless external energy is admitted.
architecture.expected_effect: The energy balance closes (input = output + losses), the car's range becomes bounded by the actual available energy, and the design no longer violates conservation of energy or the laws of thermodynamics.
architecture.falsification_test: Run the vehicle in a sealed, instrumented energy-balance cell with one measured glass of water and no other connections; if measured output work exceeds the total input energy plus the water's chemical energy, trace and identify the hidden source, and if none exists, treat the result as measurement error; if output declines as stored energy depletes, perpetual motion is falsified.
